iterations.theme: Vedran Politeo: od obraćenja i iskustva pobačaja do služenja nerođenima i iscjeljenja očeva srca

sections.subtitle: Gost koji je voditelja „napokon oženio“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predstavlja gosta Vedrana Politea na početku epizode podcasta „Redefinicija“
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **„Redefinicija“** s kanala *Muževni budite* otvara se pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija, i sveti Josip“. Voditelj odmah predstavlja gosta: **Vedrana Politea**, dugogodišnjeg člana inicijative **„40 dana za život“** i provoditelja programa **„Iscjeljenje očeva srca“**. Dodaje i osobnu napomenu da je Politeo „jedan od glavnih razloga“ zašto se on sam napokon oženio. Tu priču ostavlja za kasnije u razgovoru.

Gost zahvaljuje na pozivu i kaže da mu je drago što je u studiju. Voditelj najavljuje da će razgovarati o inicijativi i o programu, ali početak želi posvetiti nečemu osobnijem. Obojica su, kako ističe, **obraćenici**, pa ga zanima kako je izgledao Politeov život prije obraćenja, a kako nakon njega.
sections.subtitle_en: The guest who "finally got the host married"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host introduces guest Vedran Politeo at the beginning of the "Redefinicija" podcast episode
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the podcast **"Redefinicija"** from the channel *Muževni budite* opens with the greeting "Praise be Jesus and Mary, and Saint Joseph." The host immediately introduces the guest: **Vedran Politeo**, a longtime member of the **"40 Days for Life"** initiative and implementer of the **"Healing of the Father's Heart"** program. He also adds a personal note that Politeo is "one of the main reasons" why he himself finally got married. He leaves that story for later in the conversation.

The guest thanks him for the invitation and says that he is glad to be in the studio. The host announces that they will talk about the initiative and the program, but wants to dedicate the beginning to something more personal. Both of them are, as he points out, **converts**, so he is interested in what Politeo's life looked like before his conversion, and what it looked like after it.

sections.subtitle: „Ti postojiš, ali nemoj ulaziti u moj život“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo opisuje svoj površan odnos s Isusom u djetinjstvu
sections.content:
Vedran Politeo rođen je u obitelji koja je slavila Uskrs i Božić, ali u kojoj nitko nije bio praktični vjernik. Kad danas razmišlja o tom razdoblju, primjećuje da je u njemu postojala želja da upozna Isusa i da je vjerovao kako je On živ. Odnos koji je tada imao s Bogom opisuje ovako: „Okej, Ti postojiš, Ti si tu, ali nemoj ulaziti u moj život. Ja se neću Tebe dirati, neću biti kao svi ostali ljudi da Te nešto žicaju stalno.“ Isus mu je, kaže, bio poput prijatelja koji ide uz njega, dok je svatko išao svojim putem. Tako je bilo dugo, a vjera se pritom nije produbljivala.

Zanimanje za vjeru javilo se krajem osnovne, odnosno u srednjoj školi. Prijatelj kojemu je Politeo kasnije bio vjenčani kum primio je sve sakramente i pohađao vjeronauk za one koji su ih već primili. Pitao je svećenika može li dovesti nekoga, pa se Politeo, tada samo kršten, priključio skupini. Vjeronauk je vodio **Mijo Gorski**, današnji biskup. Politeo ga pamti kao čovjeka koji je lijepo radio s mladima i dopuštao različita razmišljanja i slobodnu komunikaciju kako bi im približio Isusa. Taj je vjeronauk pohađao oko godinu dana.

Unatoč tome, odlučio je ne primiti sakramente. Bile su to 90-e, nakon raspada Jugoslavije i stvaranja Hrvatske, kada su mnogi pristupali sakramentima, a voditelj dodaje: „Postali katolici.“ Politeo danas kaže da ga je tada „đavo lijepo zaveo“ mišlju „ne budi k'o svi“, jer je uvijek želio biti poseban i drugačiji.
sections.subtitle_en: „You exist, but don't enter my life“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo describes his superficial relationship with Jesus in childhood
sections.content_en:
Vedran Politeo was born into a family that celebrated Easter and Christmas, but in which no one was a practicing believer. When he reflects on that period today, he notices that there was a desire within him to get to know Jesus and that he believed that He was alive. He describes the relationship he had with God back then like this: „Okay, You exist, You are here, but don't enter my life. I won't touch You, I won't be like all the other people constantly begging You for something.“ Jesus, he says, was like a friend walking alongside him, while each went their own way. It was like that for a long time, and faith did not deepen in the process.

Interest in faith appeared at the end of elementary school, that is, in high school. A friend for whom Politeo was later the best man had received all the sacraments and attended religious education for those who had already received them. He asked the priest if he could bring someone, so Politeo, then only baptized, joined the group. The religious education was led by **Mijo Gorski**, today a bishop. Politeo remembers him as a man who worked well with young people and allowed different thoughts and free communication in order to bring Jesus closer to them. He attended this religious education for about a year.

Despite that, he decided not to receive the sacraments. Those were the 90s, after the breakup of Yugoslavia and the creation of Croatia, when many were receiving the sacraments, and the host adds: „Became Catholics.“ Politeo says today that back then the devil „nicely seduced him“ with the thought „don't be like everyone else“, because he always wanted to be special and different.

sections.subtitle: Bend, rock and roll i život bez Boga
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje razdoblje sviranja u bendu i života bez vjere
sections.content:
Umjesto sakramenata uslijedilo je sviranje u bendu, druženja i, kako sam kaže, „klasične one priče: seks, droga, rock and roll“. Kasnije se zaposlio i, prema današnjim mjerilima, bio je „okej“: savjesno je radio, ispunjavao obaveze i bio pošten.

Sve je to, ističe, živio bez Isusa. Gledajući unatrag, procjenjuje da mu je život tada bio „puno puno teži“ i da mu mnoge stvari nisu bile jasne. U tom je razdoblju imao više partnerica i djevojaka s kojima je živio.
sections.subtitle_en: Band, rock and roll and life without God
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the period of playing in a band and living without faith
sections.content_en:
Instead of the sacraments, there followed playing in a band, socializing, and, as he himself says, "those classic stories: sex, drugs, rock and roll". Later he got a job and, according to today's standards, was "okay": he worked conscientiously, fulfilled obligations, and was honest.

All of that, he points out, he lived without Jesus. Looking back, he estimates that his life back then was "much much harder" and that many things were not clear to him. In that period, he had multiple partners and girlfriends with whom he lived.

sections.subtitle: Pobačaj i spoznaja koja je došla uz usisavač
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo prepričava trenutak kada je shvatio da je pobačajem prekinut život njegova djeteta
sections.content:
S jednom od partnerica Politeo je dobio dijete. Odluku je, kaže, „nažalost prepustio njoj“, jer nije znao bolje. Malo je istraživao na internetu i ostala mu je jedna informacija: veze se nakon pobačaja često raspadnu. Priznaje da ga je najviše brinulo upravo to. Zato je možda i bio skloniji tome da se pobačaj ne napravi, ali tada nije bio svjestan da se time **oduzima ljudski život**.

Pobačaj je ipak izvršen. Nekoliko dana kasnije dogodio se trenutak kojeg se, kako kaže, točno sjeća. Usisavao je stan i odjednom mu je sinulo: „Pa da mi nismo prekinuli taj život, to bi se dijete razvilo, rodilo i bilo bi naše dijete.“ Bila je to prva spoznaja o tome kako su veliku i zlu stvar učinili.

Ta spoznaja nije odmah dovela do obraćenja, nego do raspada veze. Par se sve više udaljavao jer su oboje bježali jedno od drugoga. Razloge je, kaže, razumio tek kasnije, kad je o tome razmatrao u Isusu:

- on je **izgubio povjerenje u žene**;
- ona je izgubila **sigurnost i povjerenje u njega** kao muškarca koji ju je trebao zaštititi;
- zadatak koji su oboje trebali ispuniti ostao je neispunjen.

Zaključuje da se veza bez povjerenja u temelju ne može održati, „pusti ti i strasti i sve“.
sections.subtitle_en: Abortion and the realization that came with a vacuum cleaner
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo recounts the moment when he realized that through abortion the life of his child was ended
sections.content_en:
With one of his partners, Politeo had a child. The decision, he says, he „unfortunately left to her“, because he did not know better. He researched a bit on the internet and one piece of information stayed with him: relationships often fall apart after an abortion. He admits that this was precisely what worried him the most. That is why he was perhaps more inclined toward the abortion not being performed, but at the time he was not aware that this **takes a human life**.

The abortion was nevertheless performed. A few days later, a moment occurred that, as he says, he remembers precisely. He was vacuuming the apartment and suddenly it dawned on him: „Well, if we hadn't ended that life, that child would have developed, been born, and would be our child.“ It was the first realization of how great and evil a thing they had done.

That realization did not immediately lead to conversion, but to the breakdown of the relationship. The couple grew further and further apart because they were both running away from each other. The reasons, he says, he understood only later, when he meditated on it in Jesus:

- he **lost trust in women**;
- she lost **security and trust in him** as a man who was supposed to protect her;
- the task that both of them were supposed to fulfill remained unfulfilled.

He concludes that a relationship without trust at its foundation cannot endure, „leave aside passions and everything“.

sections.subtitle: Nevidljiva rana koja je godinama sprječavala nove veze
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava kako ga je iskustvo pobačaja godinama nesvjesno pratilo
sections.content:
Nakon raspada Politeo godinama nije mogao uspostaviti normalnu, funkcionalnu vezu. Iskustvo ga je, kako danas kaže, „proganjalo“, iako tada tako nije razmišljao. Htio je da veza „bude konačno definirana u startu“ jer nije želio sam sebi nanijeti još jednu ranu.

Naglašava da sve to nije bilo svjesno. Da je bilo, vjerojatno bi potražio pomoć. Ranu je prepoznao tek kad je zacijeljela, kada je s djevojkom mogao opet normalno razgovarati i otvoriti se, bez potrebe da sve odmah bude konačno i unaprijed poznato. Sigurnost koja se unaprijed ne može dobiti zamijenio je, kaže, „drugi oslonac“, a to je bio Isus.
sections.subtitle_en: An invisible wound that prevented new relationships for years
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains how the experience of abortion unconsciously followed him for years
sections.content_en:
After the breakup, Politeo was unable to establish a normal, functional relationship for years. The experience, as he says today, "haunted" him, although he did not think that way back then. He wanted the relationship to "be definitively defined from the start" because he did not want to inflict another wound upon himself.

He emphasizes that all of this was not conscious. If it had been, he probably would have sought help. He recognized the wound only when it healed, when he was able to talk normally with a girl again and open up, without the need for everything to be immediately definitive and known in advance. The security that cannot be obtained in advance was replaced, he says, by "another support", and that was Jesus.

sections.subtitle: Prvi vapaj Bogu: „Ja sam bitan“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo prepričava unutarnje iskustvo riječi „Ja sam bitan“
sections.content:
Pet ili šest godina nakon pobačaja na poslu se zakomplicirala jedna situacija. Politeo nije bio kriv, ali je sve upućivalo na to da će krivnja pasti na njega. „Najteže je kad si nevino osuđen“, kaže.

Tada je prvi put zavapio Bogu: „Gospodine, evo, nikad Te nisam ništa žicao, hajde sad Ti uđi u moj život i riješi ovu situaciju, jer ja više sam ne mogu.“

Gospodin ju je riješio, ali ne onako kako je on htio. Situacija se najprije dodatno zakomplicirala. U tom trenutku nešto mu se, kaže, prelomilo u srcu i iznutra je čuo ili osjetio: „Vidiš da je to sve nebitno, **Ja sam bitan**.“ Odgovorio je: „Pa da, Gospodine, Ti si bitan“ i prepustio stvar riječima „Nek' bude šta bude“.

Dan ili dva kasnije cijela se situacija rasplinula i ništa nije bilo onako dramatično kako je izgledalo. Ostalo mu je iskustvo: „Ja sam bitan.“
sections.subtitle_en: The First Cry to God: "I Am Important"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo recounts the inner experience of the words "I am important"
sections.content_en:
Five or six years after the abortion, a situation at work became complicated. Politeo was not at fault, but everything pointed to the blame falling on him. "It is hardest when you are condemned innocently," he says.

Then he cried out to God for the first time: "Lord, here, I have never begged You for anything, come now, You enter into my life and resolve this situation, because I can no longer do it on my own."

The Lord resolved it, but not in the way he wanted. At first, the situation became even more complicated. At that moment, he says, something broke in his heart and from within he heard or felt: "You see that all of this is unimportant, **I am important**." He answered: "Well yes, Lord, You are important" and surrendered the matter with the words "Whatever will be, will be".

A day or two later, the whole situation dissipated and nothing was as dramatic as it had seemed. What remained with him was the experience: "I am important."

sections.subtitle: Sakramenti kod Svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci i poziv na služenje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira Evanđelje o Sinu Čovječjem koji je došao služiti
sections.content:
Nakon toga Politeo se obratio jedinoj prijateljici iz društva koja je redovito išla u crkvu, a koja mu je danas krsna kuma: „Hajde idem s tobom u crkvu, hajmo krenuti u crkvu zajedno.“ Počeo je odlaziti na nedjeljne mise u crkvu **Svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci** i primio sakramente.

Tako je počeo njegov obraćenički život: slušanje propovijedi i čitanje Riječi Božje. Posebno ga je dotaknuo redak koji pripisuje Marku (Mk 10,45), uz koji spominje i Mateja: „Ni Sin Čovječji nije došao da bude služen, nego da služi i da život svoj dade kao otkupninu za mnoge.“

Poruku o služenju čuo je posvuda. Shvatio je da je, nakon što je upoznao Gospodina i postao svjestan koliko je toga primio na dar, došlo vrijeme da služi. Zato je molio: „Gospodine, Ti mi pokaži gdje ću služiti.“
sections.subtitle_en: Sacraments at Saint Joseph in Trešnjevka and the call to service
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes the Gospel about the Son of Man who came to serve
sections.content_en:
After that, Politeo turned to the only friend from his circle who regularly went to church, and who is today his godmother: „Come on, I'm going with you to church, let's start going to church together.” He began going to Sunday Masses at the church of **Saint Joseph in Trešnjevka** and received the sacraments.

Thus began his convert life: listening to homilies and reading the Word of God. He was particularly touched by a verse he attributes to Mark (Mk 10:45), alongside which he also mentions Matthew: „For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

He heard the message about serving everywhere. He realized that, after meeting the Lord and becoming aware of how much he had received as a gift, the time had come to serve. That is why he prayed: „Lord, You show me where I will serve.”

sections.subtitle: „40 dana za život“ sa svih strana
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo opisuje kako je posvuda nailazio na poziv inicijative „40 dana za život“
sections.content:
Odgovor je, kaže, stigao vrlo brzo. Kad bi upalio radio, čuo bi „40 dana za život“. Kad bi došao na misu, **Ante Čaljkušić** predstavljao je inicijativu i najavljivao prvu kampanju. Poziv je dolazio „sa svih strana“.

Nije poznavao nikoga iz inicijative, jer osim njegove kume nitko iz njegova društva nije išao u crkvu. Bilo mu je teško. Mučilo ga je pitanje hoće li naići na osudu, „jer i ja sam taj koji je napravio pobačaj“. Ipak je odlučio „ići u nepoznato“.

U prve dvije kampanje dolazio je na bdjenja. U trećoj ga je, kako kaže, Duh Sveti stalno poticao da učini više. Nazvao je i javila mu se **Petra**, današnja direktorica inicijative, s pozivom: „Dođi na sastanak, pa vidjet ćemo.“ Tako je počeo njegov aktivni angažman.
sections.subtitle_en: "40 Days for Life" from all sides
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo describes how he encountered the call of the "40 Days for Life" initiative everywhere
sections.content_en:
The answer, he says, arrived very quickly. When he turned on the radio, he would hear "40 Days for Life". When he came to Mass, **Ante Čaljkušić** was presenting the initiative and announcing the first campaign. The call was coming "from all sides".

He did not know anyone from the initiative, because except for his godmother, no one from his circle went to church. It was hard for him. He was troubled by the question of whether he would encounter condemnation, "because I too am the one who had an abortion." Still, he decided "to go into the unknown".

In the first two campaigns, he came to the vigils. In the third one, as he says, the Holy Spirit constantly urged him to do more. He called, and **Petra**, the current director of the initiative, answered with the invitation: "Come to the meeting, and we'll see." That is how his active involvement began.

sections.subtitle: Ne iz dužnosti, nego iz milosti oprosta
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da u inicijativu nije ušao kako bi okajao pobačaj
sections.content:
Voditelj postavlja osjetljivo pitanje: je li Politea u inicijativu dovelo upravo iskustvo pobačaja, možda kao potreba da ga opravda? Pojašnjava da ne tvrdi da je tako, ali zna ljude koji nakon pobačaja smatraju da tu ranu moraju „oprati“ molitvom ispred bolnica i domova zdravlja, kao zadovoljštinu za grijeh koji je Bog već davno oprostio.

Politeo odgovara niječno. Imao je, kaže, **milost da je u ispovijedi uoči prve pričesti zaista sve ispovjedio** i dobio Božji oprost. Gospodinu je dužan „za sve“, ali ne zbog tog grijeha. Pobačaj mu se, štoviše, činio kao moguća prepreka. U inicijativu je otišao jer je tražio Gospodina, a On je pokazivao u tom smjeru.

Osjetio je kako je s njega skinuto „ogromno breme“ i nikada nije imao potrebu taj grijeh ponovno ispovijedati. Žali, naravno, kad se sjeti, ali ističe da ostajanje u prošlosti nema smisla. Prošlost mu danas služi kao podsjetnik i kao iskustvo koje mu pomaže **razumjeti polaznike programa**. Oni se lakše otvaraju kad znaju da je pred njima jednako grešan čovjek koji ih neće osuđivati.

Prvi put se pred članovima inicijative otvorio na zajedničkoj duhovnoj obnovi. Svi su ga, kaže, prihvatili s ljubavlju i nije bilo osude. Bilo im je drago što je netko s takvim iskustvom došao među njih kao plod ljubavi i molitve.
sections.subtitle_en: Not out of duty, but out of the grace of forgiveness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that he did not enter the initiative in order to atone for the abortion
sections.content_en:
The host asks a sensitive question: did the experience of abortion bring Politeo into the initiative, perhaps as a need to justify it? He clarifies that he is not claiming that this is the case, but he knows people who, after an abortion, consider that they must "wash" that wound through prayer in front of hospitals and health centers, as satisfaction for a sin that God has already long forgiven.

Politeo answers negatively. He had, he says, **the grace that in confession on the eve of First Communion he truly confessed everything** and received God's forgiveness. He is indebted to the Lord "for everything", but not because of that sin. Abortion, moreover, seemed to him like a possible obstacle. He went into the initiative because he was seeking the Lord, and He was pointing in that direction.

He felt that "a huge burden" had been lifted from him and he never felt the need to confess that sin again. He regrets, of course, when he remembers, but emphasizes that staying in the past makes no sense. The past serves him today as a reminder and as an experience that helps him **understand the program participants**. They open up more easily when they know that before them stands an equally sinful man who will not judge them.

He opened up before members of the initiative for the first time at a joint spiritual retreat. Everyone, he says, accepted him with love and there was no condemnation. They were glad that someone with such an experience had come among them as a fruit of love and prayer.

sections.subtitle: Više od deset godina u „teškom duhovnom boju“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo govori o kapi u oceanu i licima spašene djece
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je Politeo u inicijativi od 2014., dakle više od deset godina, te da je riječ o „teškom duhovnom boju“ punom protivljenja. Pita ga što ga drži da ne odustane.

Politeo objašnjava da se u zahtjevnijim životnim razdobljima zna povući korak unatrag. Umjesto da vodi zagrebački tim, preuzme manji dio posla, primjerice koordinaciju bdjenja, jer je pozvan davati vrijeme i obitelji. Na potpuni odlazak, međutim, nikada nije ozbiljno pomišljao, iako mu takva misao zna „proletjeti kroz glavu“.

Razlog je to što zna koliko je taj rad vrijedan i koliko je života spasio, ne samo djece nego i majki i očeva koji su napravili pobačaj ili o njemu razmišljali. Citira **Majku Terezijom**: to možda jest samo kap u oceanu, ali bez te kapi ocean bi bio siromašniji. Ističe da to za njega više nije samo kap: „Ti znaš te ljude, ti vidiš ta lica, ti upoznaš tu djecu.“ Svjestan je da te djece ne bi bilo i da bi roditelji bili ranjeni da netko nije bio ondje. Taj netko slučajno je bio on, a bez njega možda ne bi bio nitko.
sections.subtitle_en: More than ten years in a "difficult spiritual battle"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo speaks about a drop in the ocean and the faces of saved children
sections.content_en:
The host reminds that Politeo has been in the initiative since 2014, therefore more than ten years, and that it is a matter of a "difficult spiritual battle" full of opposition. He asks him what keeps him from giving up.

Politeo explains that in more demanding periods of life he knows how to take a step back. Instead of leading the Zagreb team, he takes on a smaller part of the work, for example the coordination of the vigils, because he is called to give time to his family as well. However, he has never seriously thought about leaving completely, although such a thought can "flash through his head".

The reason is that he knows how valuable this work is and how many lives it has saved, not only of children but also of mothers and fathers who have had an abortion or were contemplating it. He quotes **Mother Teresa**: it may only be a drop in the ocean, but without that drop the ocean would be poorer. He emphasizes that for him it is no longer just a drop: "You know those people, you see those faces, you meet those children." He is aware that those children would not be here and that the parents would be wounded if someone had not been there. That someone happened to be him, and without him perhaps there would have been no one.

sections.subtitle: Prva molitva ispred bolnice i lekcija Šimuna Cirenca
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje molitelje ispred bolnica sa Šimunom Cirencem
sections.content:
Prvi izlazak na molitvu ispred bolnice bio je, priznaje Politeo, nezgodan, „to svatko tko je ikad išao moliti ispred bolnice može svjedočiti“. Razmišljao je o tome što će drugi reći i tko bi ga mogao vidjeti.

S vremenom su ti **ljudski obziri** nestali, jer zna zašto je ondje. Pomoglo mu je i to što je naučio argumentirati. Preporučuje knjigu **„Uvjerljivo za život“**, a voditelj dodaje da postoje dva takva izdanja. Iz njih se, kaže, čovjek može „oboružati“ informacijama i naučiti razgovarati s ljudima, pa mu više nije neugodno reći: „Stojim tu da bih obranio ove najmanje.“

Potrebu za prisutnošću na licu mjesta objašnjava primjerom **Šimuna Cirenca**: ne bi mogao ponijeti Isusov križ da je u tom trenutku molio u sinagogi, nego je morao biti ondje gdje je bio Isus. Isto vrijedi i danas: „Gdje su majke i očevi koji idu na pobačaj, tamo moramo biti. Neće oni nas doći tražiti po kapelicama.“

Kako je sve više ljudi znalo za njegov angažman, bio je spreman u miru razgovarati sa svakim tko to želi. Kad naiđe na „zid koji samo puca informacije“, zaustavi se, jer nema smisla prepucavati se s nekim tko ne želi razgovarati.
sections.subtitle_en: The first prayer in front of the hospital and the lesson of Simon of Cyrene
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares those praying in front of hospitals to Simon of Cyrene
sections.content_en:
Going out to pray in front of the hospital for the first time was, Politeo admits, awkward, „anyone who has ever gone to pray in front of a hospital can testify to that“. He thought about what others would say and who might see him.

Over time, those **human respects** disappeared, because he knows why he is there. What also helped him was that he learned how to argue the case. He recommends the book **„Persuasive for Life“**, and the host adds that there are two such editions. From them, he says, one can „arm“ oneself with information and learn to talk to people, so it is no longer uncomfortable for him to say: „I stand here to defend these least ones.“

He explains the need for being present on the spot with the example of **Simon of Cyrene**: he would not have been able to carry Jesus' cross if he had been praying in the synagogue at that moment; rather, he had to be where Jesus was. The same applies today: „Where mothers and fathers who are going for an abortion are, that is where we have to be. They are not going to come looking for us in chapels.“

As more and more people knew about his engagement, he was ready to speak in peace with anyone who wished to. When he encounters „a wall that only shoots information“, he stops, because there is no point in squabbling with someone who does not want to converse.
keywords_en: prayer in front of the hospital

sections.subtitle: Čuda koja se ne mogu opisati: od depresije do radosti
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo opisuje muškarca koji je nakon dvadeset godina oprostio sebi
sections.content:
Najsnažniji poticaj Politeu su čuda kojima svjedoči. Opisuje muškarca koji dvadeset godina nije mogao oprostiti sam sebi, a nakon programa je to uspio. „Ne zbog mene, nego zbog Gospodina, ali bio sam tu prisutan i vidio sam to čudo čovjeka koji je oživio.“

Takva iskustva, kaže, daju snagu i potvrdu da su na pravom putu jer „Gospodin čini čuda, čini ih danas, čini ih posvuda“. Priznaje i da se ponekad, unatoč svemu, pita ima li sve to smisla. Takve misli pripisuje Zlome, a brzo se vraća spoznaji da je svjedočio neopisivim čudima, „da čovjek iz depresije ide u radost“.

Voditelj dodaje da ljudi brzo zaborave čuda pa im uvijek iznova treba novi poticaj.
sections.subtitle_en: Miracles that cannot be described: from depression to joy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo describes a man who forgave himself after twenty years
sections.content_en:
The strongest encouragement for Politeo are the miracles he witnesses. He describes a man who could not forgive himself for twenty years, and after the program he succeeded. „Not because of me, but because of the Lord, but I was present there and I saw that miracle of a man who came alive.“

Such experiences, he says, give strength and confirmation that they are on the right path because „the Lord works miracles, He works them today, He works them everywhere“. He also admits that sometimes, despite everything, he wonders if all of this makes sense. He attributes such thoughts to the Evil One, and quickly returns to the realization that he has witnessed indescribable miracles, „that a man goes from depression into joy“.

The host adds that people quickly forget miracles, so they need a new encouragement time and again.

sections.subtitle: Kava koju nije popio i krunica koja je promijenila sve
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava jutro kada je ispred Vinogradske bolnice upoznao suprugu Antoniju
sections.content:
Na pitanje o najvećem plodu molitve za nerođene Politeo odgovara da bi mu bez inicijative cijeli život bio drugačiji, a najvidljiviji je dokaz njegova supruga. **Antoniju je upoznao na mjestu bdjenja.**

Priču pripovijeda u detaljima. Imao je noćnu smjenu s petka na subotu, otprilike od dva do četiri sata ujutro. Nakon nekoliko sati sna, oko devet ujutro, skuhao je kavu i namjeravao je popiti u miru. Tada je živio u **Kranjčevićevoj**, nedaleko od **Vinogradske bolnice**. U grupi se pojavila poruka da ispred Vinogradske neka žena treba pomoć. Čekao je hoće li se netko drugi javiti jer je tek bio došao kući. Na kraju je rekao: „Dobro, hajde, Gospodine, idem ja, neću popiti kavu.“

S gospođom je proveo petnaestak do dvadeset minuta i riješio što je trebalo. Budući da je već bio ondje, odlučio je izmoliti još jednu krunicu. Molio ju je s djevojkom koju dotad nije poznavao, Antonijom. Bila je to njihova prva zajednička krunica.

Tjedan dana kasnije pozvao ju je na tribinu, „kao što zovem sve ljude“, a potom je došla i na konferenciju. Voditelj se prisjeća da su „tamo pali i ćevapi“, a Politeo potvrđuje i dodaje da je i voditelj tada bio prisutan. Uslijedili su izlasci, upoznavanje i vjenčanje.
sections.subtitle_en: The coffee he did not drink and the Rosary that changed everything
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the morning when he met his wife Antonija in front of Vinogradska bolnica
sections.content_en:
To the question about the greatest fruit of prayer for the unborn, Politeo answers that without the initiative his entire life would have been different, and the most visible proof is his wife. **He met Antonija at the vigil site.**

He tells the story in detail. He had a night shift from Friday to Saturday, approximately from two to four in the morning. After a few hours of sleep, around nine in the morning, he brewed coffee and intended to drink it in peace. At that time he lived on **Kranjčevićeva**, not far from **Vinogradska bolnica**. A message appeared in the group that in front of Vinogradska a woman needed help. He waited to see if someone else would respond because he had just arrived home. In the end, he said: „All right, come on, Lord, I'll go, I won't drink the coffee.“

He spent about fifteen to twenty minutes with the lady and resolved what was needed. Since he was already there, he decided to pray one more Rosary. He prayed it with a girl he did not know until then, Antonija. That was their first Rosary together.

A week later he invited her to a panel, „as I invite all people“, and then she came to the conference as well. The host recalls that „ćevapi fell there too“, and Politeo confirms and adds that the host was also present then. Dating, getting to know each other, and marriage followed.

sections.subtitle: Ekskluziva u studiju: dijete na putu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj se iznenađeno raduje vijesti o djetetu koje dolazi
sections.content:
Govoreći o obitelji, Politeo navodi da on i Antonija danas imaju **tri rođena sina, jedno dijete na nebu i bebu koja dolazi**.

Voditelj je iznenađen: „Opa, to je nešto novo. To mi se nisi pohvalio.“ Politeo odgovara da još nije, „evo sad ti se hvalimo“. Voditelj vijest proglašava ekskluzivom i čestita mu.
sections.subtitle_en: Exclusive in the studio: a child on the way
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host is surprised and rejoices at the news of the child who is coming
sections.content_en:
Speaking about family, Politeo states that he and Antonija today have **three born sons, one child in heaven, and a baby that is coming**.

The host is surprised: „Whoa, that is something new. You didn't boast to me about that.“ Politeo replies that he hasn't yet, „here, now we are boasting to you.“ The host declares the news an exclusive and congratulates him.

sections.subtitle: Kišni dan, Sveti Toma Mor i domino-efekt apostolata
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pripovijeda kako je na Politeovu vjenčanju upoznao svoju suprugu
sections.content:
Voditelj ističe da su Politeo i Antonija jedan od brojnih parova koji su se upoznali moleći ispred bolnice. Govori o „koncentričnim krugovima“ i domino-efektu jer je i sam **na njihovu vjenčanju upoznao svoju buduću suprugu**.

Bio je to, prisjeća se, tmuran dan s jakom kišom i nije mu se dalo ići, „koliko god vas volim“, jer je mislio da tamo ionako poznaje sve. Ipak je došao i bio među prvima u crkvi. Njegova buduća supruga stigla je nekoliko sekundi kasnije. Počeli su razgovarati i nastavili se družiti u sali do kasno u noć. „Da ti nisi upoznao svoju suprugu, vjerojatno ne bih ni ja upoznao svoju“, kaže uz napomenu da se šali jer putove Gospodnje nitko ne zna.

U tome vidi kako Bog nagrađuje taj apostolat i kako mu je stalo do nerođene djece. Podsjeća na riječi koje Gospodin upućuje svojim svecima: „Ti se brini za moje, ja ću se brinuti za tvoje.“

Politeo se slaže i dodaje da je vjenčanje bilo **22. lipnja, na blagdan svetog Tome Mora**, kojega naziva zaštitnikom braka. Jutarnji pljusak kasnije je prestao i vrijeme je postalo lijepo. „Stvarno se spojilo nebo i zemlja“, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: A rainy day, Saint Thomas More, and the domino effect of the apostolate
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts how he met his wife at Politeo's wedding
sections.content_en:
The host points out that Politeo and Antonija are one of the numerous couples who met while praying in front of the hospital. He speaks of “concentric circles” and the domino effect because he himself **met his future wife at their wedding**.

It was, he recalls, a gloomy day with heavy rain and he did not feel like going, “as much as I love you all,” because he thought he already knew everyone there anyway. Nevertheless, he came and was among the first in the church. His future wife arrived a few seconds later. They began to talk and continued socializing in the hall until late at night. “If you hadn't met your wife, I probably wouldn't have met mine either,” he says, noting that he is joking because no one knows the ways of the Lord.

In this he sees how God rewards that apostolate and how He cares about unborn children. He recalls the words that the Lord addresses to His saints: “You take care of mine, I will take care of yours.”

Politeo agrees and adds that the wedding was on **June 22, on the feast of Saint Thomas More**, whom he calls the patron saint of marriage. The morning downpour later stopped and the weather became beautiful. “Heaven and earth truly joined together,” he concludes.

sections.subtitle: „Iscjeljenje očeva srca“: duhovne vježbe usmjerene na Boga Oca
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo objašnjava strukturu programa „Iscjeljenje očeva srca“
sections.content:
Na voditeljevo pitanje od čega se program sastoji Politeo objašnjava da je **„Iscjeljenje očeva srca“** zapravo niz **duhovnih vježbi za muškarce**. Polaznik čita biblijske citate i odgovara na pitanja koja ih povezuju s njegovim životom. Tako upoznaje **Boga Oca**: tko je On, koliko nas ljubi i zašto smo stvoreni. Cilj je produbiti odnos s Ocem jer, kako kaže, „taj odnos liječi“.

Pred kraj programa slijedi **životna, odnosno velika ispovijed**. Polaznik dobiva opširnu pripremu, a svećenik mu je na raspolaganju i sat ili dva za razgovor, pitanja i cjelovitu ispovijed.

Politeo za sebe kaže da je samo „poslužitelj“, a da je središte programa polaznikov susret s Gospodinom.
sections.subtitle_en: “Healing of the Father's Heart”: Spiritual Exercises Focused on God the Father
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo explains the structure of the “Healing of the Father's Heart” program
sections.content_en:
To the host's question of what the program consists of, Politeo explains that **“Healing of the Father's Heart”** is actually a series of **spiritual exercises for men**. The participant reads biblical quotes and answers questions that connect them to his life. In this way he comes to know **God the Father**: who He is, how much He loves us, and why we were created. The goal is to deepen the relationship with the Father because, as he says, “that relationship heals.”

Toward the end of the program follows a **life confession, that is, a general confession**. The participant receives extensive preparation, and the priest is available to him for an hour or two for conversation, questions, and a complete confession.

Politeo says of himself that he is only a “server,” and that the center of the program is the participant's encounter with the Lord.

sections.subtitle: Pet susreta za muškarce, tri dana šutnje za žene
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje individualni format za muškarce i grupne seminare za žene
sections.content:
Program se provodi na dva načina:

- **Individualno (jedan na jedan):** pet susreta od sat i pol do dva sata. Na svakom susretu Politeo s polaznikom prođe i prodiskutira gradivo i preda mu materijale za sljedeći susret. Taj model primjenjuje kod muškaraca jer ih je zasad malo.
- **Grupno:** trodnevni seminari od petka do nedjelje, koji se zbog većeg broja polaznica održavaju za žene. Isti se sadržaj prolazi intenzivno, u samoći i šutnji, uz ispovijed i duhovni razgovor.

Između susreta polaznik kod kuće mora pronaći mir i vrijeme da pročita odlomke iz Svetog pisma i odgovori na pitanja. Kroz njih promišlja o odnosima u obitelji, o pobačaju i o zamjeranjima drugima i sebi. Cilj je, kaže Politeo, „dotaknuti svaku točku“ i iznijeti je pred Gospodina kako bi On mogao zaliječiti rane.
sections.subtitle_en: Five meetings for men, three days of silence for women
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares the individual format for men and group seminars for women
sections.content_en:
The program is carried out in two ways:

- **Individually (one-on-one):** five meetings lasting an hour and a half to two hours. At each meeting, Politeo goes through and discusses the material with the participant and hands him materials for the next meeting. He applies that model with men because there are few of them for now.
- **In groups:** three-day seminars from Friday to Sunday, which are held for women due to the larger number of female participants. The same content is covered intensively, in solitude and silence, with confession and spiritual conversation.

Between meetings, the participant must find peace and time at home to read passages from Sacred Scripture and answer questions. Through them, he reflects on family relationships, on abortion, and on resentments toward others and oneself. The goal is, Politeo says, „to touch every point“ and bring it before the Lord so that He could heal the wounds.

sections.subtitle: I spontani i namjerni pobačaj ostavljaju ranu
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo objašnjava zašto je program otvoren i za one koji su doživjeli spontani pobačaj
sections.content:
Voditelj pita zašto je program namijenjen i muškarcima koji su doživjeli spontani pobačaj, a ne samo onima koji su sudjelovali u namjernom.

Politeo odgovara da **obje vrste gubitka nose ranu**. Spontani pobačaj moguće je prihvatiti kao volju Božju, predati ga Gospodinu, znati da je dijete s Njim i imati zagovornika na nebu. Do toga, međutim, često vodi dug put, jer se i muškarci i žene znaju osuđivati. Kao primjere navodi misli poput „to nam je treće ili četvrto dijete, kako ćemo s autom“, zatim svađu sa suprugom ili sumnju da je presudio vlastiti „nedostatak ljubavi“. Tako čovjek završi u samoosuđivanju i neriješenom odnosu s Bogom.

Potrebno je, kaže, izmiriti se s Bogom i sa sobom te prihvatiti Boga Oca koji sve zna, a sebe kao čovjeka koji ne razumije sve, ali vjeruje Bogu. Cijelu sliku vidjet ćemo tek u nebu. Do tada treba vjerovati da Gospodin zna najbolje i da nije protiv nas. Ako netko osjeća krivnju, savjetuje ispovijed i razgovor sa suprugom. Prošlost se, ponavlja, ne može promijeniti, „možeš jedino ići naprijed“.
sections.subtitle_en: Both miscarriage and induced abortion leave a wound
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo explains why the program is also open to those who have experienced a miscarriage
sections.content_en:
The host asks why the program is intended also for men who have experienced a miscarriage, and not only for those who participated in an induced abortion.

Politeo answers that **both types of loss carry a wound**. It is possible to accept a miscarriage as the will of God, surrender it to the Lord, know that the child is with Him, and have an intercessor in heaven. However, a long road often leads to that, because both men and women tend to condemn themselves. As examples, he cites thoughts such as "this is our third or fourth child, how will we manage with the car", then an argument with the spouse, or the suspicion that one's own "lack of love" was the deciding factor. Thus a person ends up in self-condemnation and an unresolved relationship with God.

It is necessary, he says, to reconcile with God and with oneself and to accept God the Father who knows everything, and oneself as a human being who does not understand everything, but trusts in God. We will see the full picture only in heaven. Until then, one should trust that the Lord knows best and that He is not against us. If someone feels guilt, he advises confession and a conversation with the spouse. The past, he repeats, cannot be changed, "you can only move forward".

sections.subtitle: „Ja ću to sam riješiti“: zašto muškarci šute
sections.screenshot_description: Gost analizira razloge zbog kojih se muškarci rjeđe javljaju na program
sections.content:
Na pitanje zašto se muškarci javljaju rjeđe od žena Politeo navodi nekoliko razloga:

- **Muška samostalnost.** Problem nije u tome da muškarci ne osjećaju odgovornost, nego u stavu „ja mogu sam to riješiti, ne treba meni pomoć“. Žene su, kaže, spremnije potražiti pomoć, makar samo nekoga tko će ih voditi kroz proces.
- **Slaba vidljivost programa.** Informacija o programu u medijima je „dosta sakrivena“ i treba je tražiti, pa se glas širi polako, od usta do usta.
- **Šutnja u muškom društvu.** Muškarci rijetko jedni drugima govore da ih muči pobačaj, jer bi odgovor mogla biti zafrkancija. Zato to potiskuju ili ne rješavaju kako bi trebalo.

Ipak, muškarci se javljaju i Politeo vjeruje da će ih zbog dobrih rezultata i preporuka biti sve više. Naglašava da nije svakome nakon pobačaja nužan program. Neki se, poput njega, s Bogom izmire već u ispovijedi. „Ali ako osjećaš nemir, potraži pomoć. Tu smo, može se to riješiti.“
sections.subtitle_en: “I will solve this myself”: why men keep silent
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest analyzes the reasons why men reach out to the program less frequently
sections.content_en:
To the question of why men reach out less frequently than women, Politeo cites several reasons:

- **Male independence.** The problem is not that men do not feel responsibility, but in the attitude “I can solve this myself, I don't need help”. Women are, he says, more ready to seek help, even if only someone who will guide them through the process.
- **Poor visibility of the program.** Information about the program in the media is “quite hidden” and needs to be searched for, so word spreads slowly, by word of mouth.
- **Silence in male company.** Men rarely tell each other that abortion troubles them, because the response could be teasing. That is why they suppress it or do not resolve it as they should.

Nevertheless, men do reach out and Politeo believes that because of good results and recommendations there will be more and more of them. He emphasizes that the program is not necessary for everyone after an abortion. Some, like him, are already reconciled with God in confession. “But if you feel unrest, seek help. We are here, this can be resolved.”

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstvo iz autobusa iz Međugorja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj prepričava svjedočanstvo brata Stjepana s hodočašća u Međugorje
sections.content:
Voditelj se nada da će epizoda pomoći da se za program čuje među muškarcima. Napominje da žene nakon trodnevnog seminara budu „doista preobražene“ i vjeruje da tako biva i s muškarcima.

Zatim iznosi osobno svjedočanstvo. Vraćajući se s nedavnog **hodočašća u Međugorje**, pozvao je putnike u autobusu da podijele ono što im je na srcu. Javio se **brat Stjepan**, za kojega voditelj nije znao da je prošao program, iako je slutio da ga nešto muči. Dok je svjedočio, bio je „lagan kô perce“, a preobrazba se jasno vidjela. Oprostio je sebi nakon, kako voditelj procjenjuje, tridesetak i više godina od pobačaja.

Voditelj zahvaljuje Bogu na programu i žali što se njegova vrijednost toliko malo poznaje, jer je utemeljen na Svetom pismu i može osloboditi od grijeha prošlosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Testimony from the bus from Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts the testimony of brother Stjepan from the pilgrimage to Međugorje
sections.content_en:
The host hopes that the episode will help spread the word about the program among men. He notes that women, after the three-day seminar, are „truly transformed“ and believes that it is the same with men.

Then he shares a personal testimony. Returning from a recent **pilgrimage to Međugorje**, he invited the passengers on the bus to share what was on their hearts. **Brother Stjepan** spoke up, whom the host did not know had completed the program, although he sensed that something was troubling him. While testifying, he was „light as a feather,“ and the transformation was clearly visible. He forgave himself after, as the host estimates, thirty or more years since the abortion.

The host thanks God for the program and regrets that its value is so little known, because it is based on Sacred Scripture and can set free from the sins of the past.

sections.subtitle: „Ne mogu vjerovati, oprostio sam si“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo s emocijom opisuje polaznika koji na zadnjem susretu kaže da je oprostio sebi
sections.content:
Na pitanje što ga se u programu najviše dojmilo Politeo opisuje trenutak koji se ponavlja. Na četvrtom susretu iz razgovora često vidi da polaznik još nije oprostio sebi i nikad ne zna hoće li do toga doći. Gospodin ga, kaže, uvijek iznova iznenadi. Na posljednji susret polaznik dođe radostan i kaže: „Nevjerojatno, ne mogu vjerovati, oprostio sam si.“

Ističe da to nije njegova zasluga nego Božja i da ga upravo to fascinira. Svjestan je, objašnjava, da čovjek koji sebi ne oprosti ne može ići u nebo. Zato se uz polaznika i sam osjeća opterećeno, nada se i moli. Program najradije provodi tijekom kampanja, kada mnogi mole na te nakane, pa je sve „još natopljenije molitvom“.

Taj trenutak opisuje kao „živo čudo“: „Mrtav bješe i oživje.“ Pred sobom vidi novog, preobraženog čovjeka, brata u Kristu koji je uskrsnuo. „To te toliko napuni energijom, vjerom, snagom. Vidiš živoga Boga.“
sections.subtitle_en: „I cannot believe it, I forgave myself“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo emotionally describes a participant who at the last meeting says that he forgave himself
sections.content_en:
When asked what impressed him most in the program, Politeo describes a recurring moment. At the fourth meeting, from conversation he often sees that the participant has not yet forgiven himself and he never knows whether it will come to that. The Lord, he says, surprises him time and again. To the last meeting the participant arrives joyful and says: „Incredible, I cannot believe it, I forgave myself.“

He emphasizes that this is not his merit but God's and that this is precisely what fascinates him. He is aware, he explains, that a person who does not forgive himself cannot go to heaven. That is why, alongside the participant, he feels burdened himself, hopes, and prays. He prefers to conduct the program during campaigns, when many pray for these intentions, so everything is „even more soaked in prayer“.

He describes that moment as a „living miracle“: „He was dead and came to life.“ Before him he sees a new, transformed man, a brother in Christ who has risen. „That fills you so much with energy, faith, strength. You see the living God.“

sections.subtitle: Straža svetog Josipa: muškarci na molitvi srijedom navečer
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje kako muškarci u Zagrebu srijedom mole Stražu svetog Josipa ispred bolnice
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da oni koji sebi oproste postaju „veliki ratnici za život“. Posebno ga se dojmio prizor muškaraca koji mole ispred bolnica u sklopu **Straže svetog Josipa**. To je sat ili dva srijedom, kad tijekom kampanje ispred bolnica i domova zdravlja mole pretežno ili isključivo muškarci, njih pet, deset, petnaest ili dvadeset.

Politeo pojašnjava da u **Zagrebu** mole srijedom, na dan posvećen svetom Josipu, **od 21 do 22 sata**. U to vrijeme zaposleni mogu doći, a djeca su već u krevetu. Najčešće mole **Krunicu svetog Josipa, žalosti i radosti svetoga Josipa**, a u korizmi i **križni put za nerođene** te druge molitve. U Zagrebu zna doći i tridesetak muškaraca.

Navodi i primjer iz jedne kampanje. Kod bolnice **Sveti Duh** nisu mogli imati mjesto bdjenja, pa su dva ili tri puta obilazili bolnicu moleći krunicu na istu nakanu.
sections.subtitle_en: Saint Joseph's Watch: men at prayer on Wednesday evening
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how men in Zagreb pray Saint Joseph's Watch in front of the hospital on Wednesdays
sections.content_en:
The host notes that those who forgive themselves become „great warriors for life“. He was particularly moved by the sight of men praying in front of hospitals as part of **Saint Joseph's Watch**. That is an hour or two on Wednesdays, when during the campaign predominantly or exclusively men pray in front of hospitals and health centers, five, ten, fifteen, or twenty of them.

Politeo explains that in **Zagreb** they pray on Wednesdays, on the day dedicated to Saint Joseph, **from 9 to 10 PM**. At that time, employed people can come, and the children are already in bed. Most often they pray the **Rosary of Saint Joseph, the sorrows and joys of Saint Joseph**, and during Lent also the **Way of the Cross for the unborn** and other prayers. In Zagreb, around thirty men can come as well.

He also cites an example from one campaign. At the **Sveti Duh** hospital they could not have a vigil site, so they walked around the hospital two or three times praying the Rosary for the same intention.
keywords_en: Way of the Cross for the unborn

sections.subtitle: Očinstvo između milosrđa i stege
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo govori o najvećem izazovu očinstva
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je Politeo, s djetetom koje očekuje s Antonijom, otac petero djece, odnosno šestero ubraja li se i ranije pobačeno dijete. Pita ga koji su najveći izazovi očinstva.

Najtežim mu je, kaže, pronaći **ravnotežu između slike milosrdnog Boga Oca** koju želi prenijeti djeci i **oštrine** kojom „otac koji ljubi sina ga kudi“. Priznaje da možda previše razmišlja o tome kako bi se plodovi trebali vidjeti ranije, iako zna da tako ne ide. Svake večeri predaje Gospodinu sve što su on i supruga pogrešno učinili da On ublaži moguće rane. Ipak, smatra da im u cjelini ide dobro.

Očinstvo opisuje kao „radost i žalost u isto vrijeme“, dok fizički napor smatra normalnim, pa i blagoslovom. Djeca mu sve vraćaju radošću, a posebno ga raduju trenuci kad vidi da se nešto „ipak primilo“. Primjer je sin koji bratu objašnjava kako nešto treba napraviti, iako to sam ne radi: „Znači da je čuo i zapamtio, samo ne odrađuje.“ Voditelj dodaje da su djeca poput spužve, pa treba paziti što se pred njima govori.
sections.subtitle_en: Fatherhood between mercy and discipline
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo speaks about the greatest challenge of fatherhood
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that Politeo, with the child he is expecting with Antonija, is a father of five children, or six if the previously miscarried child is also included. He asks him what the greatest challenges of fatherhood are.

The hardest thing for him, he says, is finding **the balance between the image of the merciful God the Father** that he wants to convey to the children and the **severity** with which „the father who loves his son chastises him”. He admits that he might think too much about how the fruits should be seen sooner, even though he knows that is not how it works. Every evening he surrenders to the Lord everything that he and his wife did wrong so that He might soothe possible wounds. Still, he considers that on the whole they are doing well.

He describes fatherhood as „joy and sorrow at the same time”, while he considers physical exertion normal, even a blessing. The children return everything to him with joy, and he is especially gladdened by moments when he sees that something „took hold after all”. An example is his son explaining to his brother how something should be done, even though he does not do it himself: „It means that he heard and remembered, he just doesn't carry it out.” The host adds that children are like sponges, so one should be careful about what is said in front of them.

sections.subtitle: Svjedočiti životom, bez glume svetosti
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo govori o autentičnom životu kao svjedočanstvu djeci
sections.content:
Voditelj ocjenjuje da roditelji Politeo postavljaju dobre temelje i da će djeca pamtiti zajedničke molitvene trenutke.

Politeo odgovara da se trude svjedočiti vlastitim životom, jer djeca ionako sve „pokupe“, i živjeti što autentičnije. „Ne treba tu glumit da smo sveci, nismo, ali trudimo se bit bolji.“
sections.subtitle_en: Witnessing through life, without pretending holiness
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo speaks about an authentic life as a witness to children
sections.content_en:
The host assesses that the Politeo parents are laying good foundations and that the children will remember the shared moments of prayer.

Politeo responds that they strive to witness through their own life, because children "pick up" everything anyway, and to live as authentically as possible. "There is no need to pretend here that we are saints, we are not, but we try to be better."

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: od latinske poslovice do Antonije Politeo
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na blic pitanja „ili-ili“ i citira latinsku poslovicu
sections.content:
Pred kraj voditelj postavlja **blic pitanja „ili-ili“** i najavljuje da su neka provokativna, a neka komična.

- **Otac koji vodi u molitvi ili otac koji sluša?** Otac koji sluša. Politeo citira latinsku poslovicu, „jedinu koju znam“, kako sam kaže: *„Noli tu imperare antequam didiceris obedire“*, odnosno ne zapovijedaj dok ne naučiš slušati. Vođenje je u redu samo ako ide uz slušanje.
- **Ante Čaljkušić ili sveti Ante Padovanski?** Sveti Ante Padovanski. „Zna se“, dodaje voditelj.
- **Program u grupi ili individualni rad?** Zasad individualni, jer je na njemu vidio rezultate, a grupni program još nije vodio pa o njemu ne može suditi.
- **Antonija Šola ili Antonija Politeo?** Antonija Politeo.
- **Poruka nade ili apel na odgovornost?** Poruka nade, „uvijek nade“, jer nada „može čovjeka iz bezdana povući“.
sections.subtitle_en: Rapid-fire questions: from a Latin proverb to Antonija Politeo
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers rapid-fire „either-or“ questions and quotes a Latin proverb
sections.content_en:
Towards the end, the host asks **rapid-fire „either-or“ questions** and announces that some are provocative, and some are comical.

- **A father who leads in prayer or a father who listens?** A father who listens. Politeo quotes a Latin proverb, „the only one I know“, as he says himself: *„Noli tu imperare antequam didiceris obedire“*, that is, do not command until you learn to listen. Leading is fine only if it goes along with listening.
- **Ante Čaljkušić or Saint Anthony of Padua?** Saint Anthony of Padua. „It is known“, adds the host.
- **A program in a group or individual work?** For now individual, because he has seen results from it, and he has not yet led a group program so he cannot judge it.
- **Antonija Šola or Antonija Politeo?** Antonija Politeo.
- **A message of hope or an appeal to responsibility?** A message of hope, „always hope“, because hope „can pull a person out of the abyss“.

sections.subtitle: „Nisi sam. Može biti bolje.“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo upućuje poruku nade muškarcima koji se bore s posljedicama pobačaja
sections.content:
Za kraj voditelj traži poruku muškarcima koji su doživjeli namjerni ili spontani pobačaj, bore se s tim i možda dvoje trebaju li se javiti na program.

Politeo odgovara kratko: **„Nisi sam. Nisi sam i može biti bolje.“** Svima koji su prošli program, kaže, bolje je nego prije, nijedan nije zažalio i svi su pronašli mir. „Koliko god sad izgleda da nema sutra, da ne može biti bolje i da si sve probao, to nije istina. Može biti bolje, i ja sam živi svjedok toga.“
sections.subtitle_en: “You are not alone. It can be better.”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo sends a message of hope to men struggling with the consequences of abortion
sections.content_en:
To conclude, the host asks for a message for men who have experienced an induced abortion or miscarriage, are struggling with it, and are perhaps hesitating whether they should reach out to the program.

Politeo answers briefly: **“You are not alone. You are not alone and it can be better.”** For everyone who has gone through the program, he says, it is better than before, none has regretted it, and all have found peace. “As much as it seems right now that there is no tomorrow, that it cannot be better, and that you have tried everything, that is not true. It can be better, and I am a living witness of that.”

sections.subtitle: Zahvala, odjava i najava epizode o novcu u crkvi
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zahvaljuje gostu i najavljuje sljedeću epizodu
sections.content:
Voditelj ocjenjuje da je to najbolja moguća završna poruka. Zahvaljuje Vedranu na gostovanju i izražava uvjerenje da je „mnogima progovorio“. Politeo zahvaljuje na pozivu i kaže da se rado odazvao.

Voditelj najavljuje sljedeću „Redefiniciju“ za idući mjesec i poziva gledatelje da se pridruže na **Patreon** profilu, gdje se nova epizoda može pogledati odmah.

U kratkom isječku iz sljedeće epizode neidentificirani sugovornik otvara temu **novca u crkvi i darivanja**. Primjećuje da novac u crkvi „uvijek ima puno veću težinu nego u birtiji“: sto kuna za rundu nikome nije problem, a dvadeset kuna u crkvi doživljava se kao velik dar.
sections.subtitle_en: Thanks, sign-off, and announcement of the episode about money in the church
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host thanks the guest and announces the next episode
sections.content_en:
The host assesses that this is the best possible closing message. He thanks Vedran for being a guest and expresses confidence that he has „spoken to many“. Politeo thanks for the invitation and says that he gladly responded.

The host announces the next „Redefinicija“ for next month and invites viewers to join on the **Patreon** profile, where the new episode can be watched immediately.

In a short clip from the next episode, an unidentified interlocutor opens the topic of **money in the church and giving**. He notes that money in church „always carries much greater weight than in a pub“: a hundred kuna for a round is no problem for anyone, while twenty kuna in church is perceived as a big gift.
